    - heading "Automatically fill in strong passwords on iPhone" [level=1]
    - paragraph: When you sign up for services on websites and in apps, you can let iPhone create strong passwords for many of your accounts.
    - paragraph:
      - text: iPhone
      - link "stores the passwords in the Passwords app":
        - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/use-passwords-iphd18e98624/27/ios/27
      - text: or your chosen password manager, and fills them in for you automatically, so you don’t have to memorize them.
    - paragraph:
      - emphasis: "Note:"
      - text: If you use a third-party password manager, you can accept the strong passwords suggested by the password manager or enter your own. Your passwords are saved in the password manager.
    - paragraph: "Instead of requiring you to sign in with passwords, participating websites and apps support these alternatives:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - emphasis: "Sign in with Apple:"
          - text: Lets you use your Apple Account to sign in, and limits the information shared about you. See
          - link "Sign in with Apple":
            - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/sign-in-with-apple-iph238921d37/27/ios/27
          - text: .
      - listitem:
        - paragraph:
          - emphasis: "A passkey:"
          - text: Lets you use Face ID or Touch ID to securely sign in without using a password. See
          - link "Use passkeys to sign in to websites and apps":
            - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/use-passkeys-to-sign-in-to-websites-and-apps-iphf538ea8d0/27/ios/27
          - text: .
    - heading "Create a strong password for a new account" [level=2]
    - region:
      - paragraph: Depending on the website or app, creating a strong password and saving it to the Passwords app usually consists of steps similar to these.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: On the new account screen for the website or app, enter a new account name.
          - paragraph: For supported websites and apps, iPhone suggests a unique, complex password.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: "Do one of the following:"
          - list:
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - emphasis: "Choose the suggested password:"
                - text: Tap Use Strong Password.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - emphasis: "Edit the suggested password:"
                - text: Tap Other Options, tap Edit Strong Password, tap the password text field, then make your changes.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - emphasis: "Get a different strong password:"
                - text: Tap Other Options, tap Edit Strong Password, then tap the suggested password.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - emphasis: "Get a strong password consisting of only numbers and letters:"
                - text: Tap Other Options, then tap No Special Characters.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - emphasis: "Get a strong password that’s easy to type:"
                - text: Tap Other Options, then tap Easy to Type.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - emphasis: "Make up your own password:"
                - text: Tap Other Options, then tap Choose My Own Password.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: To copy the password so you can paste it into a Confirm Password field if asked, tap Other Options, then tap Copy Strong Password.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph:
            - text: To
            - link "securely add and keep notes":
              - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/view-your-passwords-and-related-information-iph3ee1dd6e7/27/ios/27#iphd9f2cd623
            - text: about recovery key information, security questions, PIN numbers, and similar details, enter them in the Notes field.
          - paragraph: To view the notes later, go to the Passwords app on your iPhone, tap All, then tap the account.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: To later allow iPhone to automatically fill in the password for you, tap Yes when you’re asked if you want to save the password.
    - heading "Automatically fill in a saved password" [level=2]
    - region:
      - paragraph: Depending on the website or app, signing in with your saved password usually consists of steps similar to these.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: On the sign-in screen for the website or app, tap the account name field.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: "Do one of the following:"
          - list:
            - listitem:
              - paragraph: Tap the account suggested at the bottom of the screen or near the top of the keyboard.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - text: Tap
                - img "the Password AutoFill button"
                - text: ", tap Other Passwords, then tap an account."
          - paragraph:
            - text: The password is filled in. To see the password, tap
            - img "the Show Password Text button"
            - text: .
      - paragraph:
        - text: To enter an account or password that isn’t saved, tap
        - img "the Keyboard button"
        - text: on the sign-in screen.
    - heading "Turn Password AutoFill on or off" [level=2]
    - region:
      - paragraph: Go to Settings > General > AutoFill & Passwords, then turn on or off AutoFill Passwords and Passkeys.
      - paragraph: You can automatically fill passwords from up to three passwords apps.
    - heading "See also" [level=3]
    - link "Automatically fill in SMS passcodes on iPhone":
      - /url: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/automatically-fill-in-sms-passcodes-iphc89a3a3af/27/ios/27

Request bytes are limited to what Playwright exposes; not_exposed does not establish body absence or multipart file coverage.
Network content reads settle within 5 seconds each and never wait for unfinished responses or refetch them.
Playwright scenario events do not expose request initiator stacks; receipt order does not prove causality.
Storage values are hashed only after declared-secret redaction.
